# Status Trio attribution

Blinker's status icons and parts of its status-reading and audio-control implementation include material adapted from [Status Trio](https://github.com/lingyired/status-trio), Copyright 2026 lingyired, under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

The source revision is [`d1672377a172ee4cb4af53d5054610c407c0d34f`](https://github.com/lingyired/status-trio/tree/d1672377a172ee4cb4af53d5054610c407c0d34f). [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE) are unchanged copies from that revision. The license text also matches the [Apache Software Foundation's official text](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt).

## Scope and modifications

Blinker adapts the battery ring, network indicator, volume dots or arc, and Dock artwork. The integration reads local battery, network and audio state and uses public CoreAudio APIs to adjust volume, mute and switch output devices; the default input device is shown with its own volume and mute controls. Current-output Bluetooth metadata can change the icon. The panel also reports VPN tunnels, system VPN services and the system proxy endpoint, and — after an explicit opt-in and a Location Services grant, which macOS requires to un-redact the SSID — the current Wi-Fi network name. The panel lists paired Bluetooth devices with their classes, per-channel battery levels and reported signal strength from the system Bluetooth report, and — behind a second opt-in and a Bluetooth grant — scans nearby BLE devices for the standard Battery Service. Blinker does not import Status Trio's complete application, updater, analytics, DDC support, VPN management beyond that read-only status row, device connect actions, or HID-usage kind refinement.

Beyond upstream parity, Blinker adds its own battery-controller details (cycle count, health, temperature and charge/discharge power), interface throughput and local/public IP rows (the public-IP lookup is opt-in and the panel's only outbound request), Bluetooth signal-strength subtitles, and — behind a separate opt-in sharing the Bluetooth privacy grant — A2DP codec subtitles and per-device disconnect, plus panel density and per-row subtitle controls. These additions are Blinker-original and are not derived from Status Trio.

Adapted source files carry a modification notice identifying their origin. Blinker-specific settings control placement, appearance, panel sections and device ordering. Left click opens the status panel by default, with App Rules as an alternative; right click retains the menu.

The upstream paths below are relative to `Sources/StatusTrioCore/` at the pinned revision. Blinker paths are relative to `Sources/BlinkerApp/`.

| Blinker file | Upstream source | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `MenuBar/TrioIconGeometry.swift` | `UI/Icon/StatusIconGeometry.swift` | Retains battery, Ethernet, volume-dot and volume-arc geometry; removes unused upstream geometry. |
| `MenuBar/TrioIconRenderer.swift` | `UI/Icon/StatusIconRenderer.swift`; `Models/StatusMappings.swift`, `Models/BatteryIconOptions.swift`, `Models/VolumeIconOptions.swift`, `Models/RingStrokeStyle.swift` | Adapts colors, scale, weight, battery numbers, network and current-output Bluetooth symbols, and volume styles to Blinker's configuration and explicit unknown states. The glyph renderer is static; Blinker supplies separate charging effects. |
| `MenuBar/DockIconRenderer.swift` | `UI/Icon/DockIconRenderer.swift` | Preserves the Dock artwork proportions with configurable backgrounds, including transparency, and Blinker's shared glyph renderer. |
| `MenuBar/SystemStatusMonitor.swift` | `Store/SystemStatusStore.swift`, `Monitoring/BatteryMonitor.swift` | Rewrites event and lifecycle handling with one bounded reader, restart guards and a timeout; retains no upstream store or application controller. |
| `MenuBar/SystemStatusReader.swift` | `Monitoring/BatteryMonitor.swift`, `Monitoring/WiFiMonitor.swift`, `Monitoring/WiFiStatusReader.swift`, `Monitoring/AudioStatusReader.swift` | Adapts battery parsing, signal thresholds and serial reads; classifies personal hotspots, ad-hoc connections and Internet Sharing; reads the Wi-Fi name only behind an explicit opt-in and Location grant. |
| `MenuBar/SystemVPNProbe.swift` | `Monitoring/VPNProbe.swift`, `Monitoring/VPNMonitor.swift`, `Models/VPNStatus.swift` | Adapts the tunnel-interface classifier, system VPN service lookup and proxy-endpoint parsing into a single read-only probe folded into the snapshot read; no separate monitor. |
| `MenuBar/WiFiNameAuthorizer.swift` | `Monitoring/WiFiNameAuthorizer.swift` | Adapts the CoreLocation authorization wrapper for Wi-Fi name access unchanged in behavior. |
| `MenuBar/SystemAudioStatusReader.swift` | `Monitoring/VolumeMonitor.swift`, `Audio/CoreAudioOutputChannelElements.swift` | Adapts default-output volume reads and channel handling, with bounded buffers and listener cleanup; derives Bluetooth audio appearance from public transport and terminal metadata, without DDC. |
| `Audio/CoreAudioBackend.swift`, `Audio/SystemAudioHardware.swift` | `Audio/CoreAudioOutputController.swift`, `Monitoring/AudioInputMonitor.swift` | Adapts output-device enumeration and public CoreAudio volume, mute and selection operations, adding serialization, cancellation, bounded buffers and device-identity guards; adds default-input volume and mute with the same write-time identity checks. |
| `Bluetooth/SystemBluetoothProfiler.swift`, `Bluetooth/SystemBluetoothModels.swift` | `Monitoring/BluetoothDeviceController.swift`, `Monitoring/BluetoothBatteryReader.swift` | Adapts the system-profiler paired-device read, connected-first address deduplication, per-channel battery parsing and ghost detection into one folded device model with a bounded subprocess and a last-good cache; no HID refinement. |
| `Bluetooth/BluetoothDeviceKind.swift` | `Models/BluetoothDeviceKind.swift` | Retains the minor/major wording tables and ordered substring rules; flattens the nested kind enum to one level for icon selection. |
| `Bluetooth/BluetoothLEScanner.swift`, `Bluetooth/BluetoothLEScanner+GATT.swift` | `Monitoring/BluetoothLEBatteryScanner.swift`, `Monitoring/BluetoothLEBatteryParsing.swift` | Adapts the scan window, automatic cadence, candidate queue, concurrency and cooldown policy, the GATT session state machine and the model-read publish gate; replaces the controller-driven lifecycle with a single enable switch. |
| `Bluetooth/BluetoothLESupport.swift` | `Monitoring/BluetoothLEBatteryAdvertisement.swift`, `Models/BluetoothNearbyDeviceMerge.swift`, `Models/BluetoothMobileDeviceModel.swift` | Retains the Battery-Service and Apple Continuity candidate rules (name required on the Continuity route) and the exact-name fold of Apple mobile readings onto the paired list; simplifies the mobile-model table to family prefixes. |

The monitoring and audio-control code is a Blinker-specific rewrite informed by those implementations, not an unchanged copy of the upstream controllers. Blinker's snapshot and preference models, settings and panel views, presentation, scroll handling, charging animation, `Audio/SystemAudioController.swift` and `Audio/SystemAudioModels.swift` are new integration code. `MenuBar/SystemBatteryDetails.swift`, `MenuBar/SystemNetworkActivity.swift` and `Bluetooth/BluetoothConnectionDetails.swift` implement the beyond-parity depth items above and contain no upstream material.

## Distribution

The app bundle includes this directory at `Contents/Resources/ThirdParty/StatusTrio/`. The license view in About displays this provenance, the original NOTICE and the full Apache 2.0 text without a network connection. Packaging includes these files and release validation compares them byte for byte with the release source.

Blinker as a whole remains GPL-3.0-only. The incorporated Status Trio material retains its Apache 2.0 notices and terms; this does not relicense the upstream project. The [GNU license list](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.html#apache2) identifies Apache 2.0 as compatible with GPLv3.
